domain_characteristics.detection_complexity: moderate to high due to text obfuscation, social engineering tactics, and variability in phishing content
data_characteristics: includes URLs, obfuscated words, and social engineering language

common_indicators: presence of suspicious or obfuscated URLs in email body
use of urgent or enticing subject lines related to health, finance, or job offers
inclusion of misspellings, grammatical errors, and nonsensical filler text to evade detection
attack_signatures: phishing emails often contain calls to action urging users to click links or provide personal information, e.g., 'Click Here!', 'Guaranteed results', 'Update your payment information'
use of brand impersonation or spoofed reputable sources, e.g., fake CNN newsletter style with embedded URLs
insertion of random or nonsensical word sequences (e.g., 'epicranium excellente ethylhexyl') to confuse text-based filters
technical_markers: URL presence rate: >1 suspicious URL per email body often indicates phishing
high frequency of health or medication-related keywords in phishing samples (e.g., 'Viagra', 'medications', 'herbal breakthrough')
subject line length typically short and generic or overly promotional (e.g., 'Job Vacancies', 'Guaranteed Erection Fast')
attack_vectors: email phishing via crafted email content with embedded URLs and social engineering text
exploit_techniques: social engineering to induce clicks or data entry
text obfuscation with filler nonsense words

typical_behaviors: benign emails contain technical, professional, or community discussion content without urgent calls to action
subjects are descriptive and relevant to the email body content, e.g., mailing list discussions, technical problem reports
email bodies have coherent, well-structured text with minimal spelling or grammatical errors
baseline_metrics: average URL count per email body close to zero or only legitimate URLs
absence of suspicious keywords related to health products, financial urgency, or job offers
subject line length moderate, typically descriptive and specific (e.g., '[Python-Dev] GSoC student introduction')
operational_patterns: emails often contain signatures, contact information, or references to external resources relevant to the discussion
benign emails show consistent formatting and professional tone
absence of unsolicited requests for personal information or payment updates
normal_thresholds: URL count per email body < 1 for benign
absence of known phishing keywords such as 'Viagra', 'payment suspended', 'click here'
subject line length > 5 characters and contextually relevant

current_threats: phishing campaigns targeting users with health-related scams
financial fraud attempts via payment suspension notices
job offer scams soliciting personal information
brand impersonation of trusted news sources (e.g., CNN)
emerging_patterns: use of nonsensical filler text to bypass text-based filters
increased use of multi-source phishing datasets indicating diverse phishing tactics
combining social engineering with URL obfuscation to evade detection
risk_factors: users clicking on embedded malicious URLs
lack of user awareness of phishing indicators
insufficient email filtering for obfuscated or disguised phishing content
threat_landscape.threat_sophistication: medium sophistication with basic evasion techniques such as obfuscation and social engineering but lacking advanced polymorphic or zero-day exploits

detection_rules: flag emails containing more than one URL with domain reputation below threshold
detect presence of health-related or financial urgency keywords combined with call-to-action phrases
identify emails with nonsensical or random filler words sequences exceeding a token threshold
monitor subject lines with generic or overly promotional language combined with suspicious body content
monitoring_recommendations: implement URL reputation checks and sandboxing of links
monitor for sudden spikes in emails with payment or account suspension themes
use NLP techniques to detect incoherent or obfuscated text patterns
track source identifiers to identify phishing campaigns from known datasets or sources
threshold_suggestions: alert if URL count per email body > 1 and URLs are not whitelisted
trigger alerts for emails containing >3 suspicious keywords related to health or finance
flag emails with >10% of body tokens identified as gibberish or nonsensical
consider subject lines shorter than 5 characters or containing only generic terms as suspicious when combined with other indicators
pattern_matching: use regex patterns to detect common phishing phrases like 'Click Here', 'Guaranteed results', 'Update your payment information'
pattern match URLs with known phishing domains or suspicious TLDs
apply fuzzy matching to detect brand impersonation in subject lines and body text
detect repeated use of filler nonsense words as evasion technique
